messages:
Liam (Acme): hey team :wave: onboarding hit a weird spike of 429s during SDK init. first few calls succeeded, then it just started failing across pods. tokens look fine in our system. any ideas?

Ava (CS): thanks for flagging — can you paste the sdk version + a short excerpt of the client logs? also which region?

Liam (Acme): SDK v1.8.3, region eu-west-1. logs show repeating init calls: 200,200,200,429,429,429 across ~30s. we use short-lived app tokens (rotated via our auth).

Sam (SDK Eng): can you share the exact init call pattern? is your app creating many processes/containers that call SDK.init simultaneously on start?

Liam (Acme): yes, our deployment scales up ~20 containers during deploy, each runs startup sequence that calls `SDK.init()` then does a quick health ping. here's a trimmed log block:

```
POST /v1/sdk/init 200 12ms
POST /v1/sdk/init 200 15ms
POST /v1/sdk/init 200 9ms
POST /v1/sdk/init 429 3ms
POST /v1/sdk/init 429 2ms
POST /v1/sdk/init 429 2ms
```

We also have a retry helper with tiny jitter. snippet: 

```
function start() {
  sdk.init(opts).catch(() => setTimeout(start, 10));
}
start();
```

(not production, but shows what we shipped)

Sam (SDK Eng): aha — that tight retry loop combined with a scale-up burst will cause a thundering herd against our rate windows. the 10ms retry is too aggressive. can you change to an exponential backoff with jitter (e.g., 200ms -> 5s) and add a small random startup delay per replica?

Priya (SE): another quick win: cache the token locally (shared memory or disk) so concurrent inits reuse the same token instead of all hitting token refresh paths. also consider `SDK.init({ maxConcurrentInits: 2 })` on the next SDK release if you need to gate init concurrency.

Liam (Acme): makes sense, will modify. can you recommend a temporary mitigation on Redwood side? we need to finish onboarding tonight.

Ava (CS): I can request a temporary ramp of the per-key rate window for your account for 2 hours while you roll out the fix. I'll open a support ticket and note the timeline. can you confirm approximate deploy time?

Liam (Acme): rolling now, expect 10 minutes to finish. thanks.

support-bot: Support ticket #22108 created for account "Acme" — request: temporary per-key rate uplift (eu-west-1) for 2 hours.

Sam (SDK Eng): follow-up checklist for you:
- switch retry to exponential backoff with full jitter (`base=200ms, cap=5000ms`)
- add randomized startup jitter (0-1500ms) across replicas
- cache tokens locally and avoid per-replica refresh during startup
- instrument `init` success/failure counters and send a one-off dump of those to us if issues persist

Liam (Acme): implemented backoff + jitter and token cache, redeployed. initial telemetry looks much cleaner, no 429s after the next 30s. will keep monitoring. :thumbsup:

Ava (CS): perfect — leaving the support ticket open for the 2 hour window and will cancel uplift if we see no more 429s. tagging for postmortem notes.

Priya (SE): i'll follow up tomorrow with a small SDK example showing safe init patterns for containerized apps that we can add to the docs.

Liam (Acme): thanks everyone — big help.
